title: Simple word classes at the lowest stage
statement: At the lowest stage, name words only by a few simple classes and devices, such as noun, verb or metaphor, and keep finer terms for the top stage.
example: One knowledge base allows six simple labels at its first stage and keeps terms such as tricolon and past participle for its third.
detail: A Grade 9 unit's knowledge base limits its first stage to six simple classes, noun, verb, adjective, adverb, repetition and metaphor, and lets its third stage name tricolon, paradox and past participle (`g9/sources/1. Act 1 - Knowledge Base - Overview.csv`, line 138). Its quality pass found a word labelled a verb that is a past participle, kept the simpler label at the first stage and left the precise term for the third (line 149).
against: The case was flagged, not resolved (`g9/sources/1. Act 1 - Knowledge Base - Overview.csv`, line 149), and another record asks lessons to simplify without saying anything false; whether calling a past participle a verb is false is arguable.

evidence.quote: Simple classes only at Stage 1: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, repetition, metaphor. Stage 3 may name tricolon, paradox, past participle.
